## A. Egyptian exports: identify an ARIMA model

```r
egypt <- global_economy |>
  filter(Code == "EGY")

egypt |> autoplot(Exports) +
  labs(y = "% of GDP", title = "Egyptian Exports")

egypt |>
  features(Exports, unitroot_ndiffs)

egypt |>
  gg_tsdisplay(Exports, plot_type = "partial")

fit <- egypt |>
  model(ARIMA(Exports))

report(fit)
gg_tsresiduals(fit)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What to notice

- Decide if the raw series looks stationary and whether differencing is required.
- Compare visual evidence (plot, ACF/PACF) with unit root outputs.
- Check whether residual diagnostics support the fitted ARIMA model.
:::

## B. Central African Republic exports: compare candidate models

```r
caf <- global_economy |>
  filter(Code == "CAF")

caf |> autoplot(Exports)

caf_fit <- caf |>
  model(
    arima210 = ARIMA(Exports ~ pdq(2,1,0)),
    arima013 = ARIMA(Exports ~ pdq(0,1,3)),
    stepwise = ARIMA(Exports),
    fullsearch = ARIMA(Exports, stepwise = FALSE, approximation = FALSE)
  )

glance(caf_fit) |>
  arrange(AICc) |>
  select(.model:BIC)

caf_fit |>
  select(fullsearch) |>
  gg_tsresiduals()
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What to notice

- Which models are competitive by AICc and why?
- Does the best information-criterion model also pass residual checks?
- Explain your final model choice for forecasting.
:::
